To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the quality and safety of care in the operating theatre is dependent on the interdependent and interrelated behaviours and attitudes of the team members, the organizational culture, the physical and social environment and the quality of the communication.
the following factors are associated with patient safety and quality of care: 1) shared vision and goals; 2) reliable systems and procedures; 3) good teamwork; and 4) optimal communications.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying the key determinants of quality and safety and how to optimize these for improved outcomes.

the development and evaluation of a patient safety framework that can be used to identify, understand, measure and mitigate the risks to patient safety and quality of care in the perioperative environment.
understanding the nature, extent and causes of variability, error and harm in the perioperative environment, with the ultimate aim of improving patient safety and outcomes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are many factors that determine patient safety and quality of care, and that it is a core value of the nursing profession.
there is no one single solution to patient safety.
there are a number of key elements which are necessary to achieve patient safety, and that these elements are not new.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the key to improving patient safety is to understand how the human mind works and how to harness this knowledge to create a safe environment.
we have identified the key factors that influence patient safety and have developed a framework to support and guide perioperative teams to deliver quality care and improve patient outcomes.
patient safety is a core value of the profession and that the nursing workforce has a key role to play in delivering safe and quality care.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the most important factor for achieving safe care is the ability to recognize and address error.
patient safety in the peri-operative setting is not just a nursing issue.
the human condition is the greatest threat to quality care and patient safety and the greatest barrier to quality improvement.
